The 1951–52 season was '''[[Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]]''''s [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|49th season]] in existence and the club's 20th consecutive season in the top flight of Spanish football.

==Summary==
During summer, President Santiago Bernabéu closed the arrivals of Zarraga<ref>{{cite web|url=https://as.com/futbol/2012/04/03/mas_futbol/1333404049_850215.html|title=Zarraga is dead, a madridista with 5 European Cups|publisher=as.com|date=3 April 2012|accessdate=1 July 2020|language=Spanish}}</ref> forwards Joseíto<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.abc.es/sociedad/abci-nino-queria-futbolista-200707140300-1634230712597_noticia.html|publisher=as.com|title=A kid who wanted to be football player|language=Spanish|date=14 July 2007|accessdate=1 July 2020}}</ref> reinforcing the offensive line and Uruguayan head coach [[Hector Scarone]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://revistauncanio.com.ar/picado/un-viejo-conocido-del-madrid/|publisher=revistauncanio.com.ar|title=An old familiar man to Real Madrid|language=Spanish|accessdate=1 July 2020}}</ref> On 30 March 1952, the team played a friendly match against Colombian side [[Millonarios]], marking the debut of Argentine striker [[Alfredo Di Stéfano]] in front of Madrid fans, and President Santiago Bernabéu started negotiations for his transfer to the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://as.com/futbol/2016/07/28/mas_futbol/1469697390_056937.html|title=Madrid won the little cup|publisher=as.com|date=29 July 2016|accessdate=1 July 2020}}</ref> The squad reached a decent third place, five points below Champions [[FC Barcelona|CF Barcelona]].

During June, the squad reached the [[1952 Copa del Generalísimo]] semi-finals, being defeated after two matches by [[Valencia CF]] with a global score of 2–3. [[Pahiño]] clinched the first spot on the top scorers of La Liga with 28 goals.
